slides.headline: Your Gift Card Finances Starbucks
slides.subheadline: Follow prepaid dollars into corporate funding and forgotten-balance revenue.

designSystem.typography: Condensed editorial headlines; readable sans-serif body; monospace kickers, dates and tabular numerals.
designSystem.geometry: 0px corners; crisp 1px hairlines; square markers; no shadows, pills, thick accent borders or rounded progress indicators.
designSystem.citationRendering: Retain inline citation markers in the storyboard; typeset their references in the footer source ledger.
designSystem.productionNotesRendering: Production notes are verification instructions, not additional slide copy.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw an axonometric coffee cup as an engineering cutaway, occupying half the canvas. Rectangular dollar tokens enter immediately through the lid into a chamber labeled 'customer prepayments'. A narrow lower outlet labeled 'coffee later' ends at a cup silhouette. A separate dashed accounting conduit passes through a square valve labeled 'estimated nonredemption' into a revenue ledger. Render loyalty Stars in a detached, hatched compartment with no cash-flow connection. Use 1px section lines, dimension ticks and coordinate marks. The reservoir is a timing metaphor, not a segregated bank account; never label it insured deposits.
slides.sourceNote: The card agreement defines loaded value as prepayment and promises easier, more rewarding shopping. The annual report records loads as deferred revenue and describes breakage recognition.​

slides.headline: Convenience Makes Prepayment Feel Harmless
slides.subheadline: The shopping benefits are real; liquidity still leaves.

items.title: NO FEES
items.body: **No activation, service, dormancy or inactivity fees**.

telemetry.label: Activation, service, dormancy and inactivity fees.

slides.svgBlueprint: Create an exploded physical gift-card engraving inside the hero panel. Its top layer carries a simple coffee glyph; the lower layer exposes a one-way prepayment arrow. Place a calendar outline with no terminal date in the expiration panel and four empty fee cells in the fee panel. Stars sit in a separate perforated tray, visibly distinct from dollar tokens. Use sharp rectangular frames and 1px connector lines, not app screens or interface controls.
slides.sourceNote: These promises apply to the Starbucks Card and its balance. Do not extend the no-expiration promise to loyalty Stars.

slides.headline: That Balance Is Not Cash
slides.subheadline: Cards, loyalty obligations and royalties complicate the headline.

items.title: ANNUAL FLOW
items.body: Annual deferrals **include Stars, not just cash**.

metric.label: Million; current Nestlé deferred revenue; September 28, 2025.

slides.svgBlueprint: Integrate a narrow exploded-ledger drawing above the rows. Show three separate transparent rectangular folios: dollar-token card obligations, star-hatched loyalty obligations and a Nestlé royalty contract. Bracket cards and Stars together without estimating their individual proportions. Draw the annual-flow arrow outside the closing-balance bracket to distinguish a yearly flow from a point-in-time stock. Never draw all three as liquid inside the customer-prepayment reservoir.

productionNotes.accountingGuardrail: Neither a combined card-and-loyalty liability nor a broader deferred-revenue caption is a standalone customer-cash measurement. Do not subtract Nestlé royalties and call the remainder gift-card cash.
productionNotes.rollForwardCitation: Complete fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 card-and-loyalty roll-forwards.
productionNotes.rollForwardNotes: Other changes primarily reflect foreign-currency translation. Approximately $1.6 billion of the combined liability was current at each year-end.

slides.headline: Cash Arrives Before The Coffee
slides.subheadline: Prepayment funds Starbucks before product revenue gets recognized.

items.title: CASH FIRST
items.body: Loading creates **deferred revenue**, not immediate sales.

items.title: COFFEE LATER
items.body: **Redemption generally triggers revenue** for purchased goods.

items.title: ACCOUNTING VALVE
items.body: **Estimated nonredemption** becomes revenue proportionately with redemptions.

telemetry.label: Year; historically, most stored-value cards redeemed within this period.

slides.svgBlueprint: Extend the cup reservoir vertically alongside the spine. At LOAD, solid red arrows carry dollars through the lid into 'customer prepayments'. At REDEEM, the lower outlet releases a coffee silhouette while a corresponding ledger entry reduces the obligation. At ESTIMATE, a dashed line passes through a square accounting valve into revenue, synchronized visually with redemption marks. Add a small branching line for applicable unclaimed-property remittances. Keep the Stars compartment detached. The breakage valve represents accounting recognition, not money disappearing from an individual card.

productionNotes.recognitionRule: Starbucks estimates nonredemption from historical redemption patterns and recognizes breakage in proportion to redemptions, incorporating applicable unclaimed-property remittances.
productionNotes.criticalDistinction: No expiration does not prevent breakage recognition. Do not depict an expiration fee, interest income, or automatic cancellation of the customer's balance.​

slides.headline: Unredeemed Value Becomes Reported Revenue
slides.subheadline: The filing separates breakage across two store channels.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw two sharply outlined accounting channels labeled 'company-operated' and 'licensed'. Each terminates at a square ledger node, with numerals typeset separately from the drawing. Join them using a 1px summation brace beneath the monumental total. Place a tiny cutaway reservoir valve at the brace origin to connect this evidence to the previous slide. No profit icon, cash pile or proportionally sized reservoir: the total measures recognized revenue.

productionNotes.calculation: $200.4 million + $22.0 million = $222.4 million. The total is calculated from the two disclosed revenue categories.
productionNotes.comparativeCitation: Disclosed components and calculated totals; revenue, not financing savings or net profit.

slides.headline: Reload Friction Can Preserve Prepayments
slides.subheadline: Starbucks gains payment timing; advocates challenged reload friction.

items.title: PAYMENT RESTRICTIONS
items.body: Allegedly **no split payments** for in-app card orders.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw a plan-view reservoir with a residual-value pocket and a return pipe labeled 'reload'. An open coffee outlet sits beyond the pocket; a dashed route illustrates the coalition's alleged reload cycle. Use four square numbered callouts corresponding to the four entries, without recreating a present-day app interface. Give the entire alleged mechanism dashed outlines; reserve solid lines for the established prepayment reservoir. Keep Stars outside the cash circuit and avoid depicting deliberate intent as proven.
slides.footer: DATED ALLEGATIONS · NOT FINDINGS OR TODAY'S INTERFACE

productionNotes.attribution: The Washington Consumer Protection Coalition submitted these allegations on December 19, 2023. The complaint is evidence of what was alleged, not an adjudication.
productionNotes.minimumDistinction: The complaint distinguishes a $10.00 actual minimum from the $15.00 lowest displayed option and $25.00 default.
productionNotes.institutionalIncentive: Starbucks describes its card program as supporting convenient payment, gifting and increased store-visit frequency. Its accounting independently establishes payment before redemption; the complaint is not needed to prove that mechanism.
productionNotes.causationGuardrail: Do not attribute the calculated fiscal 2025 breakage total to these alleged practices or suggest that this complaint verifies the current interface.

slides.headline: Interest-Free Funding. Not A Bank.
slides.subheadline: You surrender liquidity; Starbucks gains timing and breakage.

items.title: CUSTOMER TRADEOFF
items.body: You receive **no interest or FDIC insurance**.

items.title: LEGAL LIMITS
items.body: Cash-redemption and unclaimed-property laws **still constrain prepayments**.​

slides.svgBlueprint: Resolve the recurring reservoir into a simplified architectural elevation. Label the main chamber 'retail prepayments'. Keep the coffee outlet and dashed breakage-recognition valve visible. Add a separate lawful cash-redemption exit with a square jurisdiction marker, not an unrestricted withdrawal tap. Draw the Stars compartment outside the chamber. Below, align three square verification marks with the ledger rows; no bank façade, shield of protection or alarmist disappearing-money effect.

productionNotes.refundRule: Card balances generally cannot be refunded or redeemed for cash unless law or the agreement permits.
productionNotes.californiaRule: SB 22, Chapter 207, approved October 1, 2025, increased the statutory cash-out threshold from less than $10 to less than $15, operative April 1, 2026, and expressly included electronic gift cards.
productionNotes.specifiedExemption: The cash-out provision exempts qualifying certificates donated to nonprofit or charitable organizations without consideration when they bear a noncash-redemption disclaimer in at least 10-point font.
productionNotes.finalGuardrail: Interest-free customer financing is the economic interpretation of retail prepayment without customer interest. Do not characterize Starbucks as an entirely unregulated bank, combined liabilities as pure cash deposits, or breakage revenue as quantified net profit.​​
